column1: # SOUP register — IEC 62304 §5.3.3 / §8.1.2, ISO/IEC 27001 A.8 supply chain
# Every *direct* dependency of this crate must appear here with a purpose
# and a safety/security relevance note. `src/compliance/soup.rs` merges
# these annotations with the real dependency graph from Cargo.lock to
# produce the CycloneDX SBOM at GET /api/compliance/sbom, and its unit
# tests fail the build when a direct dependency is missing (or when an
# entry names a package that is no longer depended on).
# Scope note: this service is a **governmental** case registry (benefits,
# legal, social services, complaints, appeals, investigations). It is not
# health software and carries no IEC 62304 safety classification — see
# spec/12-compliance.md. The register is kept because a dependency
# inventory with a stated purpose per item is worth having on its own
# merits, and because ISO/IEC 27001 supply-chain and configuration
# management want exactly this artefact. "Safety-relevant" below means
# relevant to the correctness and confidentiality of case data, not to
# Transitive dependencies are listed in the SBOM but are NOT individually
# annotated. Stating that boundary is more honest than implying we have
# Blank lines and lines starting with '#' are ignored.

column2: Web application framework: boot, routing, config, background workers, model error types.
column3: Security-relevant. Owns request routing and the middleware stack, so a defect could bypass the auth/ABAC guard that gates every case read.

column2: Serialization framework for every wire type and the stored JSONB payload.
column3: Security-relevant. A mis-serialized payload could corrupt a stored case or an audit snapshot.

column2: JSON encoding/decoding, and the canonical form the audit hash chain digests.
column3: Security-relevant. Key ordering (BTreeMap, preserve_order disabled) is load-bearing for chain verification across a JSONB round-trip; a reordering would report untouched rows as tampered.

column2: Async runtime.
column3: Availability-relevant. Runtime failure means service unavailability, not data disclosure. Industry standard.

column2: Async methods in traits (loco Hooks, SeaORM migrations).
column3: Not security-relevant. Compile-time macro only, no runtime behaviour of its own.

column2: HTTP server, extractors, and response types underneath loco.
column3: Security-relevant. Header and path extraction feed the auth guard and the purpose-of-use disclosure context.

column2: Structured logging and spans, including the audit_checkpoint witness lines.
column3: Security-relevant. The no-secrets-in-logs invariant is enforced at call sites, not by this crate.

column2: Log formatting, filtering, and the JSON layer.
column3: Security-relevant. Misconfiguration could emit more case detail than intended; log level is deployment-controlled.

column2: Pattern matching in payload validation.
column3: Security-relevant. Used only on length-capped input (SEC-M1 caps), which bounds the catastrophic-backtracking risk.

column2: This crate's own sea-orm-migration migrator (path dependency).
column3: Security-relevant. Owns the schema, including the audit_logs compliance columns and entity_links. First-party code, not third-party SOUP.

column2: Async ORM and query builder over PostgreSQL.
column3: Security-relevant. All persistence, including the audit trail and the record-level ABAC reads, goes through it. Query construction uses its typed builders, not string concatenation.

column2: Timestamps, durations, and the microsecond truncation the audit chain depends on.
column3: Security-relevant. Chain digests bind created_at as epoch microseconds; a precision change would break verification of existing rows.

column2: Declarative validation attributes.
column3: Not security-relevant today: the substantive rules live in src/validation.rs, which does not use it.

column2: Public record identifiers (pid) and EntityRef ids.
column3: Security-relevant. v4 generation uses the OS RNG; a guessable case id would weaken the IDOR posture that record-level ABAC otherwise enforces.

column2: Embeds static assets (Swagger UI) into the binary.
column3: Not security-relevant. Serves documentation assets only; no case-data path.

column2: Global allocator for MUSL static builds.
column3: Availability-relevant. An allocator defect would be a process-wide fault. Enabled only for the musl target.

column2: Metrics registry and text-exposition rendering for /metrics.prom.
column3: Not security-relevant. Counters only; the endpoint exposes no case data.

column2: SHA-256 for the tamper-evident audit hash chain and record content hashes.
column3: SECURITY-CRITICAL. The integrity evidence rests on this implementation. RustCrypto, widely audited; constant-time is not required for an unkeyed hash.

column2: Second integrity digest alongside SHA-256 for the audit chain and record hashes.
column3: SECURITY-CRITICAL. Kept for structural diversity: SHA-3 is a sponge construction, unrelated to SHA-256's Merkle-Damgard chaining, so a cryptanalytic advance against one design family does not transfer. FIPS 202, so it carries NIST standing while being structurally independent of SHA-2. RustCrypto, same maintainers as sha2.

column2: Keyed integrity MACs (HMAC-SHA256) with HKDF domain separation, key sourcing, zeroization, and key generation (path dependency).
column3: SECURITY-CRITICAL. The MAC is the only stored integrity value an adversary holding just the database cannot forge — the SHA-256 and SHA-3 digests are unkeyed with published pre-image formats. Extracted into one shared crate rather than copied per service precisely because a key-handling defect in a copy would not announce itself: it would make MACs forgeable while every test stayed green. First-party code with its own test suite, including golden vectors cross-checked against an independent HKDF implementation.

column2: Canonical matching engine; its Case type is also this service's API DTO (path dependency).
column3: Security-relevant. A false match can conflate two distinct cases, merging one subject's record into another's — a confidentiality failure, not just a data-quality one. First-party code with its own spec and property tests.

column2: Cross-service EntityRef URN and EdgeKind registry for the subject_of (case → person) edge (path dependency).
column3: SECURITY-CRITICAL. The subject_of edge asserts that a named person is the subject of a government case — the highest-sensitivity fact this service holds (cross-service-linking.md §10). Edge-kind validation here is what stops an arbitrary edge type being written.

column2: Offline PASETO v4.public verification and the shared ABAC policy engine (path dependency).
column3: SECURITY-CRITICAL. Every authentication and authorization decision depends on it, including the record-level checks and masking obligations that gate case reads. First-party code with its own forgery and policy-property test suites.

column2: Serialises tests that mutate process-wide environment variables.
column3: Test-only. Not present in a release artefact.

column2: Parameterised test cases.
column3: Test-only. Not present in a release artefact.

column2: Snapshot assertions.
column3: Test-only. Not present in a release artefact.

column2: Mints throwaway Ed25519 keys so the token-verification path is tested in-process.
column3: Test-only. Not present in a release artefact; the test seed is not a secret.

column2: Mints PASETO v4.public tokens in the auth unit tests.
column3: Test-only in this crate. The production verification path lives in authentication-verifier.

column2: Encodes test key material into the JWK-shaped key set.
column3: Test-only. Not present in a release artefact.

column2: Temporary key files for the MAC key-file sourcing tests.
column3: Test-only. Not present in a release artefact.

column2: Embedded full-text search index over case records (src/search/): the title/subject/identifier search surface and the duplicate detector's candidate blocking.
column3: Indirect. It never decides case content: the database is the source of truth and every hit is resolved against it (through the same record-level ABAC concealment as every other read path), so a stale or wrong index degrades retrieval (a case a search fails to surface) rather than corrupting a record or bypassing authorization. A missed hit can still mean a duplicate case is created, which is why the index is rebuildable (`cargo loco task search_reindex`) and rebuilt automatically when empty.
